answer: A durable defence is a reputation grove grown slowly, not bought instantly. Every agent stakes a bond and earns standing only through months of verifiable, useful work recorded in a public atlas of attestations, so trust is tied to history rather than to a fresh keypair. A Sybil signal check then flags clusters that share funding, timing, or identical behaviour and quarantines them until each proves independent work. Forging one trusted identity is cheap, but forging a hundred costs a hundred bonds plus months of compute and labour, which makes large-scale fakery unprofitable.
